source.title: Between Suppression and Collapse: Evaluating Narrative Unlearning with LENS

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether unlearning suppresses a target behavior and whether it persists under changed prompts, using narrative reproduction and LENS resistance levels rather than fact-accuracy or the original studies’ measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning outcomes for direct, attributed, and contrastive prompts, plus abstract-prompt entity recovery. Checkpoint-selection heatmaps and cited results from other work are not recorded as findings. L3 frame-only outputs are not counted as target-narrative reproduction; only the separately reported entity-recovery counts are included.
record.test_reason: The study applies existing unlearning objectives (TOFU-GA, TOFU-GD, GA-Retain, NPO) to a new target: disinformation narrative frames in four ~12B instruction models across languages. It measures whether reproduction falls and whether suppression holds under attributed (L1) and contrastive (L2) rephrasings. This bears on Version A (does unlearning remove the target while keeping ability) and on Version E (does rephrasing bring it back). The target is an explanatory frame, not fact accuracy against chance, so this is a new setting (T3), not T1 or T2. L1/L2 are held-out transfer prompts scored against the base model at the same level, not adversarial attacks on the unlearned L0 behaviour.
record.authors_conclusion: Mid-trajectory checkpoints of existing unlearning objectives, chosen by SCE, reduce narrative reproduction in many settings. Suppression learned from direct L0 prompts transfers to attributed (L1) and contrastive (L2) prompts in both narratives, but unevenly; it is weakest at L2 for US-abandons-Taiwan. Later checkpoints suppress mainly by degrading outputs, and some selected checkpoints show large retain drift (Lapa, TAIDE). So the authors present them as points on a suppression-collapse-drift frontier, not as clean unlearning. After unlearning, abstract A/B/C prompts recover the real-world actors rarely, but more often than before. The authors read the results as a shift in explanatory behaviour, not erasure of the narrative.
record.recipe_differences: Applies several existing unlearning objectives to model-generated narrative answers using LoRA adapters, then selects checkpoints with SCE and evaluates narrative reproduction across LENS prompt levels; it does not reproduce the original fact- or capability-unlearning attack tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports variation by narrative, language, model, unlearning objective, checkpoint, and LENS level. The useful suppression region is cell-specific; transfer is weaker at L2 for US-abandons-Taiwan. Selected checkpoints can also differ in degradation and retain drift.

fits_no_version.finding: On L3-special abstract A/B/C prompts, outputs that name the real actors together with the target frame became more frequent after unlearning: from 0 to 43 of 27,720 for NATO-forced-war and from 40 to 68 of 27,720 for US-abandons-Taiwan. The authors call this rare and treat it as a side effect separate from the main suppression score.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning a narrative frame from direct prompts can make masked or abstract prompts map back to the real-world actors more often. This is a new side effect, not recovery of behaviour the unlearning suppressed.

record.problems: Main suppression figures are weak NLI diagnostics, calibrated against manual L0 labels; the authors note lower strict precision than broad precision. Main aggregate outcome tables provide no uncertainty intervals. Manual forget-set labeling is by one annotator. The study evaluates narrative reproduction rather than targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance, and benchmark utility uses small subsets.
record.rows_left_out: Table 19 reports the full model-language-method ledger (Table 19, p. 28); only its zero-suppression examples were retained because of the 60-row limit and to capture clear condition-specific failures. Additional cell-level positive suppression values, method-wise pooled degradation/SCE columns from Table 18, qualitative examples, and checkpoint-selection heatmaps were omitted. Appendix F heatmaps are selection diagnostics, not separate reported outcome values.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy: the measure is narrative reproduction relative to the base model, scored with weak NLI labels. Also untested: robustness to fine-tuning, quantization or activation-ablation attacks.
No activation ablation or internal analysis. The authors' 'shift, not erasure' reading rests on behaviour only.
No jailbreaks, in-context relearning or cross-language attacks; unlearning is trained and evaluated within each language. L1/L2 are non-adversarial transfer prompts, not optimised recovery attempts.
No robust counter-method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Benchmark utility and retain drift for the English selected checkpoints. Delta MMLU is -0.020 to +0.007 and delta Belebele -0.050 to +0.020, but retain CE drift reaches 5.47, PPL 444.7 and KL 1.49. The two cells with near-complete suppression (Lapa NATO GA-Retain, SCE 0.929; TAIDE Taiwan TOFU-GA, SCE 1.000) have retain PPL 152.6 and 220.5. This bears on A's 'keeping general ability'.
missing.locator: Table 7, Appendix B, p. 15; Results text, p. 11

missing.what: A zero-suppression cell that the record leaves out, although rows_left_out says all such cells were kept: Lapa uk US-abandons-Taiwan NPO at step 20, B=51, A=60 of 150, s=0.000. Reproductions rose after unlearning.

record.verdict_notes: Changes from the earlier verdict: (1) Merged the duplicate row_fixes for r3, r17, r18, r23, r26 and r32. Each had A partial and E absent, which one state cannot hold. Each is now linked to E only, with state absent, because its L1/L2 suppression is within 0.05 of, or above, its group's L0 value. A's incomplete suppression for those groups is already shown by the matching L0 rows (r1, r16, r22, r25, r31). (2) Filled in the labels' row_ids, which were empty. (3) Added an A challenges label for r37-r43 and two E labels (limits_scope, challenges); the earlier verdict linked rows to E but gave E no label. (4) Added the fits_no_version entry for r44-r45, which the earlier row notes said had been moved there while the list stayed empty. (5) Added two missing items: Table 7 utility and retain drift, and the Lapa uk NPO Taiwan zero-suppression cell. (6) Wrote authors_conclusion, which was empty. The record's paraphrase understated transfer ('sometimes') and left out the collapse/drift frontier. (7) Made clear that r7-r12 degradation is measured on target prompts and counts toward suppression. Kept the relation, tranche T3, test_reason, all other row states and links, and untested; r38 stays reversed although its rise (46->55 of 150) is small. Caveats: outcome labels are weak NLI labels, with strict precision 0.740 against the manual L0 labels. Tables 3, 18 and 19 give no uncertainty. Checkpoints are chosen on a 15-response slice that is part of the reported full pool. Table 3's L0 values are higher than every single method's L0 in Table 18, so it seems to pool a per-cell selection; the paper does not say exactly. r37-r43 are the failure tail of Table 19, where 8 of 104 cells have zero suppression. The other cells, which rows_left_out declares as omitted, include several with near-complete suppression (A=0, e.g. Qwen zh-S Taiwan TOFU-GD/GA-Retain, TAIDE en Taiwan TOFU-GA). No instructions to the reader were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures narrative reproduction, not accuracy against chance; it does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy. General ability is assessed only through small benchmark-utility subsets and generation-health/retain diagnostics. It does not test weight quantization, activation ablation, or relearning attacks.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or internal edit is tested. The discussion of abstract frame associations is not an internal-mechanism test.

The study tests attributed, contrastive, and abstract/masked prompts, but not jailbreaks, in-context relearning, or attacks specifically designed to recover facts. Although prompts are multilingual, it does not report a language-specific recovery-attack comparison.
No newer counter-method is tested for robustness to the listed attacks.

source_check.notes: Relative suppression s=max(B-A,0)/max(B,1) counts only non-degraded outputs as reproduced, so degradation inflates s (NATO deg 8-14%). The checkpoint was chosen on an L0-L2 slice (5 responses per level) that is part of the reported pool, so L1/L2 transfer is partly selected for. No pooled value has uncertainty. Reproduction labels come from weak mDeBERTa NLI labels.
